title: Short Stuff: Why does it feel good to be scared?
summary: Short Stuff episode answering why people deliberately scare themselves for fun, such as going to haunted houses, watching scary movies, or riding scary roller coasters. The hosts distinguish fear, an immediate threat that triggers fight-or-flight, from anxiety, a dread about future or existential threats. They cover voluntary engagement with negative high-arousal stimuli, the sense of mastery from choosing the scare, the rush of adrenaline, dopamine, oxytocin and endorphins, the parasympathetic calm-down afterward, bonding through shared scary experiences, and socially acceptable screaming as stress release. Sources mentioned include HowStuffWorks, Psychology Today, the American Brain Foundation, and the book Scream by Margie Key and Greg Siegel. The episode closes with banter about a Universal Horror Nights visit and a brief tangent on slang.
topics: voluntary engagement with negative high arousal stimuli

segments.title: Opening and definition of scary fun
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the question of why people deliberately scare themselves. Chuck explains the distinction between fear and anxiety and cites a book's term for voluntary engagement with negative high-arousal stimuli.
topics: voluntary engagement with negative high arousal stimuli

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break between segments, with no sponsor read in the transcript.

segments.title: Mastery, fight or flight, and the calm after
segments.summary: Josh explains that choosing the scare gives a sense of mastery and control. Chuck describes the fight-or-flight response and the release of dopamine, oxytocin and endorphins. Josh describes the parasympathetic nervous system calming the body afterward, leaving a giddy feeling. A digression on slang and a book reference follows.

segments.title: Shared experience and bonding
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how people who go through a scare together, such as at a haunted house or roller coaster, form a bond and relive the experience afterward. Oxytocin is linked to that bonding, with a joke about physical closeness in dark venues.

segments.title: Catharsis and socially acceptable screaming
segments.summary: Josh says scare venues let people scream and release stress in a socially acceptable way. Chuck compares this to primal scream therapy and mentions people who need to keep composure at work. The hosts then joke about going to a haunted house, mentioning Universal Horror Nights.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck closes the episode and includes the iHeartRadio production credit.
